meta.title: PS5 Recorder
meta.description: One button in the sidebar for the whole PS5 pipeline: record the capture card, finalize the cut and upload it to YouTube. Type the game name and press Start recording — the plugin launches OBS and records at 1080p60 H.264 into MKV, with Pause / Resume / Stop while recording. On Stop it stream-copies the MKV to MP4 (no re-encode), renames it to your convention (game | EP number, e.g. GTA VI | EP 03), extracts a thumbnail and uploads it to your own YouTube channel with configurable title, description, tags, visibility, playlist and auto-incrementing episode numbers; uploads are resumable, retryable and the queue survives a restart. Requirements: OBS installed and able to preview the capture card, ffmpeg installed (brew install ffmpeg), HDCP turned off on the PS5 (Settings › System › HDMI › Enable HDCP), and pressing Prepare OBS once (it aligns OBS recording path/container/encoder/frame rate; if OBS was running, quit and reopen it so the WebSocket server setting takes effect). Automatic upload also needs a free Google Cloud OAuth Desktop-app client created once — prefer the Personal mode introduced in 2026 to avoid 7-day token expiry, enable YouTube Data API v3, then paste the client ID and secret into Settings › Upload and press Connect YouTube; the plugin requests youtube.upload and youtube scopes (upload plus playlist insert). Recordings live in ~/Movies/PS5 (configurable), plugin state in ~/.dsh/ps5-recorder/state.json and OAuth tokens in ~/.dsh/ps5-recorder/youtube-tokens.json (mode 0600, local only); the HTTP API listens on loopback and validates Origin, and never returns secrets to the page. Upload quota is 100 videos.insert calls per Cloud project per day. Limitations: macOS only; requires capture-card signal; does not delete recordings or set YouTube synthetic-media / paid-promotion declarations; disabling the plugin removes the panel and auto-upload but leaves OBS recording settings in place.
